column1: # Tier 2 group A countries (France and its overseas departments, Monaco, Belgium, the Netherlands, Luxembourg, Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Liechtenstein).
# Columns: code, country line (English; UPU country sheets and UPU print it so), line style, languages, postcode form, accepted country prefixes before a postcode,
# printed prefix, house number position, longest address line before abbreviations are used (0 = no limit), spaces between postcode and locality, street type sets.
# Line style afnor: capitals, no accents, no punctuation (La Poste, Guide pratique courrier 2026, p. 19-21; SP 8855 volume 2, section 3.1). Line style plain: lines as written, locality in capitals.
# Postcode form: 5d, 4d, or 4d2l (four digits, a space, two letters). House number position: first, last or both.
# Maximum line: La Poste 38 characters (SP 8855, 3.1; UPU France sheet); bpost 50 characters (Belgian template, 3. Representation rules).

# Tier 2 group B (the United Kingdom with Jersey, Guernsey and the Isle of Man, Ireland, Spain, Portugal, Italy, San Marino, the Vatican, Malta, Andorra). A twelfth column names the profile that decides how the reader writes a line.

# Postcode forms: uk (UPU United Kingdom sheet, six formats and GIR 0AA, own line after the post town), eircode (UPU Ireland sheet, 3 + 4 characters, own line last), pt (UPU Portugal sheet, 4 digits, a dash, 3 digits), mt (UPU Malta sheet, 3 letters, a space, 4 digits, after the locality), ad (UPU Andorra sheet, AD and 3 digits), 5d (Spain, Italy, San Marino, Vatican).

# Profiles: uk, ie (delivery lines and locality in capitals, UPU Ireland examples), es (commas kept before the floor and door, UPU Spain sheet), pt (capitals, UPU Portugal sheet), it (capitals, no punctuation from the street line on, UPU Italy sheet), sm, va (Italian system, lines as written), mt, ad.
